ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha=9c4ca95ea6e8 (2026-05-05T09:51:18Z) introduced a synchronous database migration runner in checkout-service v2.3.1 via changes to checkout-service/migration/runner.go. On pod startup, MigrationRunner.runPendingMigrations() executes all pending SQL migrations on the main goroutine before the HTTP server is ready to serve, but after the health probe endpoint (:8080/healthz) is already bound and returns 200. This causes the Kubernetes liveness/readiness probe to pass and api-gateway to route live traffic to the pod while all 20 DB connection pool slots are held by the long-running migration (0042_backfill_order_totals.sql backfilling 4.2M rows, ~44s). Every inbound request immediately exhausts the connection queue, resulting in 503 errors for the full duration of the migration. Additionally, the migration state is not correctly persisted, meaning every pod restart re-runs the same migrations.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately roll back checkout-service to the previous stable image (sha=a4553ea12420 or earlier) using: kubectl rollout undo deployment/checkout-service. 2. Verify error rate drops below 5% and P99 latency returns to baseline (<500ms) after rollback. 3. In the follow-up fix for migration/runner.go: (a) move migration execution to a pre-startup init container or a separate migration Job so the main pod does not accept traffic until migrations complete; (b) ensure the health probe endpoint returns 503/not-ready while migrations are running; (c) fix the migration state persistence bug so completed migrations are not re-run on restart. 4. Add a load test covering large-table backfill migrations before re-deploying.
